findings.evidence: `Invariants.lean:202` declares `invariants R C M g ≃ Hom R C R M`; `Comodule/Hom.lean` provides `instance instModule : Module R (Hom R C M N)`, and Mathlib's analogous `Representation.invariantsEquivRepHom` is a `≃ₗ[k]`.
findings.fix: Import/use the comodule Hom module API and expose this as a linear equivalence `invariants R C M g ≃ₗ[R] Hom R C R M`, with the same forward/inverse simp lemmas.
findings.issue: `invariantsEquivHom` is only a plain `Equiv`, so the public universal property forgets the `R`-linear structure of both `invariants R C M g` and the comodule Hom-space.

findings.evidence: `Invariants.lean:202` has `@[expose] noncomputable def invariantsEquivHom`; lines 219-233 already provide downstream-facing simp lemmas for applying the equivalence and its inverse.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]`; keep the body opaque and rely on `invariantsEquivHom_apply`, `invariantsEquivHom_symm_apply_coe`, and any added linear-equivalence simp lemmas.
findings.issue: `@[expose]` on `invariantsEquivHom` makes consumers depend on the implementation body even though characteristic lemmas are provided for both directions.

summary: The basic invariants API is present, but the universal-property declaration exposes the wrong public interface and unnecessarily exposes its body.
